books.title: Our Mutual Friend
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.desc: A body pulled from the Thames, a fortune made from rubbish heaps and a will with strange conditions set off Dickens's last completed novel about money and London.
about: Gaffer Hexam and his daughter Lizzie make a living from the river Thames, and one night they bring in a drowned man believed to be John Harmon, heir to a fortune made from dust heaps on condition that he marry Bella Wilfer, a young woman he has never met. With Harmon apparently dead, the money passes to the kindly, unlettered Mr and Mrs Boffin, who take the pretty and mercenary Bella into their home, while a mysterious young man appears in the Wilfer household and Lizzie attracts the attention of two very different men.

Dickens builds a vast panorama of London, from riverside poverty to the empty display of fashionable society, around one central question: what money can make of life. Satire, mystery, comedy and darkness mix in a large cast that includes the scheming ballad-seller Silas Wegg and the troubled schoolmaster Bradley Headstone.
Our Mutual Friend was published in monthly instalments from May 1864 to November 1865. It was the last novel Dickens completed; he died in 1870 leaving The Mystery of Edwin Drood unfinished.

books.title: Barchester Towers
books.author: Anthony Trollope
books.desc: A new bishop, his formidable wife and his scheming chaplain arrive in Barchester, and the cathedral town erupts in a comic struggle for power and a wealthy widow's hand.
about: When the old bishop of Barchester dies, the new bishop, Dr Proudie, arrives with his domineering wife and his oily chaplain, Obadiah Slope. Archdeacon Grantly and the traditional clergy of the diocese prepare for battle. Meanwhile Eleanor Bold, the widowed daughter of the gentle Mr Harding, finds herself pursued by suitors, including Mr Slope himself, as the eccentric Stanhope family, among them the captivating Signora Neroni, returns from Italy and adds to the confusion.

Trollope turns church politics, ambition and courtship into one of the great comedies of English fiction. His narrator comments freely and wittily on the characters, and the struggle between Mrs Proudie and Mr Slope for control of the bishop is among his most famous creations.
Barchester Towers was published by Longmans in 1857, two years after The Warden, as the second of Trollope's six Chronicles of Barsetshire.

books.title: Daniel Deronda
books.author: George Eliot
books.desc: A proud young woman gambling in a German spa and a generous young man searching for his own origins cross paths in George Eliot's last and most ambitious novel.
about: The novel opens at a roulette table in a German resort, where the beautiful and self-assured Gwendolen Harleth notices a young Englishman watching her: Daniel Deronda, the ward of the wealthy Sir Hugo Mallinger, who knows nothing of his own parents. When her family loses its money, Gwendolen considers marriage to the cold and calculating Henleigh Grandcourt. Deronda, meanwhile, saves a young Jewish singer, Mirah, from despair, and is drawn into London's Jewish community, where he meets the visionary scholar Mordecai.

Eliot weaves two stories together: a sharp portrait of English high society and of a woman who marries for money, and Deronda's search for his identity and purpose. The novel's sympathetic portrayal of Jewish life, culture and hopes for a national homeland was unusual and controversial at the time.

Daniel Deronda was published in eight instalments from February to September 1876. It was George Eliot's last completed novel and the only one set in the society of her own day. It was soon translated into German and Dutch and is said to have influenced early Zionist thinkers.

books.title: Washington Square
books.author: Henry James
books.desc: In old New York, a plain, shy heiress is courted by a charming young man, and her clever, cold father is sure he only wants her money.
about: Catherine Sloper lives with her father, the wealthy and respected Dr Austin Sloper, in a fine house on Washington Square in New York. She is gentle, dutiful and shy, and her father, who still mourns his brilliant wife, finds her a disappointment. When the handsome and charming Morris Townsend begins to court her, encouraged by her romantic and meddling aunt Mrs Penniman, Dr Sloper is convinced that the young man is after Catherine's fortune.

James tells a short, finely balanced story of a daughter caught between the will of her father and the attentions of her suitor. With quiet irony and deep psychological insight, he explores pride, money, love and the slow growth of Catherine's own strength of character.

Washington Square was serialised in 1880 in the Cornhill Magazine and in Harper's New Monthly Magazine, and published in book form the same year. It was adapted for the stage in 1947 and became the 1949 film The Heiress, directed by William Wyler.

books.title: The House of Mirth
books.author: Edith Wharton
books.desc: Beautiful, well-born but penniless, Lily Bart must marry money to keep her place in New York high society, but she cannot bring herself to pay the price.
about: Lily Bart is admired by everyone in New York society for her beauty and charm, but she has no money of her own and depends on a wealthy aunt. To keep her place among the rich, she knows she must marry well, yet each time an advantageous match is within reach, something in her holds back. Her friendship with Lawrence Selden, a lawyer of modest means who stands slightly apart from society, offers her another view of life.

Wharton gives an unsparing portrait of the wealthy New York of the 1890s, its rules, gossip, gambling debts and cruelty to those who fail. The novel explores how a woman raised only to be decorative is trapped by money, reputation and her own choices. Its portrayal of the Jewish financier Simon Rosedale reflects the antisemitic prejudices of the society, and of the time, it describes.

The House of Mirth was serialised in Scribner's Magazine from January 1905 and published as a book on 14 October 1905. It was an immediate bestseller and established Wharton as a major American novelist. Its title comes from Ecclesiastes: "the heart of fools is in the house of mirth."
books.author_short: American novelist and short-story writer (1862–1937), author of The House of Mirth, Ethan Frome and The Age of Innocence.
author_long: Edith Wharton was born Edith Newbold Jones in New York City on 24 January 1862, into a wealthy old New York family. In 1902 she built The Mount, her house in Lenox, Massachusetts. She later settled in France, where she died on 11 August 1937.

Wharton wrote more than forty books, including novels, stories and works on architecture, gardens, interior design and travel. Her best-known novels include The House of Mirth (1905), Ethan Frome (1911) and The Age of Innocence, which won the 1921 Pulitzer Prize and made her the first woman to receive the prize for fiction.
